1.2.3.15-f58.text: hoc est cur palles, cur quis non prandeat hoc est?

translations.literal: this is why you are pale, why someone does not lunch, this is?
translations.note: In Persius the question is asked of the philosopher who goes pale and skips meals over his studies. Burton applies it to the poor rewards of divines. The standard text reads 'hoc est quod palles?' ('is this what you go pale for?'); Burton has 'cur palles'. The sense is the same.

source.author: Persius
source.basis: sidenote "Pers. Sat. 3."; the line is Persius 3.85

translations.text: Is this why you grow pale? Is this why a man goes without his dinner?

translations.literal: This is why you are pale, why someone does not dine — is this it?
translations.note: Persius, Satires 3. The question is a taunt at the scholar's pallor and fasting. Burton's English that follows renders only the gist.

burton_span.exact: Do we macerate ourselves for this?

translations.text: Is this why you are pale? Is this the reason why anyone should go without his dinner?
